facts.text: Ronan was originally called Spring Creek and renamed in 1893 after Major Peter Ronan, superintendent of the Flathead Indian Reservation.
The city sits on the Flathead Indian Reservation, which was established by the 1855 Hellgate Treaty between the U.S. and the Bitterroot Salish, Upper Pend d'Oreille, and Lower Kutenai tribes.
Ronan lies about 12 miles south of Flathead Lake, with the Mission Mountains to its east and Ninepipe National Wildlife Refuge just five miles to the south.
The public library in Ronan is the Ronan City Library, serving the community’s reading needs.
The local FM station KKMT broadcasts from Ronan, keeping residents tuned to regional news and music.
The town’s sports teams are called the Chiefs for boys and the Maidens for girls, reflecting local school spirit.
